column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Bound the battle” is rendered “began the battle.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Kingship” is rendered “the rule,” and “descendants” as “sons.” NASB supplies “by.”
“Masters” is rendered “master.”

“Empty men, sons of worthlessness” is rendered “worthless men … scoundrels,” and “weak of heart” as “timid.” “Did not show himself strong before them” is rendered “could not hold his own against them.”
“You are saying” is rendered “you intend,” and “show yourselves strong before” as “resist.” “In the hand of” is rendered “through.”
“To fill his hand” is rendered “to consecrate himself”; “a young one of cattle” is not rendered separately. “Not gods” is rendered “what are no gods.”
NASB supplies “attend to their work” for “in the work.”

“Making smoke” is rendered “burn,” and “in the morning in the morning” as “every morning.” “The row of bread” is rendered “the showbread is set”; NASB supplies “is ready.” “Duty” is rendered “charge.”
NASB supplies “our”; “the trumpets of the alarm to sound the battle signal” is rendered “the signal trumpets to sound the alarm.”
“Caused to go round the ambush” is rendered “had set an ambush”; NASB supplies “Israel.”
“There was to them the battle before and behind” is rendered “they were attacked both front and rear.” “Blowing a trumpet on trumpets” is rendered “blew the trumpets.”
“Sounded the battle signal” is rendered “raised a war cry”; NASB supplies “then it was that.” “Defeated” is rendered “routed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“A great striking” is rendered “a great slaughter.”
“Humbled” is rendered “subdued,” “were strong” as “conquered,” and “depended on” as “trusted in.”
NASB reads “Ephron,” the name read aloud, for the written “Ephrain.” “Daughters” is rendered “villages,” and NASB supplies “several.”
“Retained strength again” is rendered “did not again recover strength.”
“Strengthened himself” is rendered “became powerful.”
“Matters” is rendered “acts,” and “record” as “treatise.”
